source_dataset.dataset_title: Mars MGS MOLA - MEX HRSC Blended DEM Global 200m
source_dataset.recommended_citation: Fergason, R. L., Hare, T. M., & Laura, J. (2018). HRSC and MOLA Blended Digital Elevation Model at 200m v2. Astrogeology PDS Annex, U.S. Geological Survey.

component_attribution.MOLA: CC0, as stated on the USGS product record
component_attribution.HRSC: CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO, as stated on the USGS product record

checksum.reason: The original source is 11,384,463,908 bytes. Its header metadata was inspected without reading or hashing the full source raster.

processing_environment_observed_at_manif.note: Versions below were observed in the available project Python environment during provenance capture. Historical product-generation environments are not embedded in the existing slope raster.

processing_pipeline.input_product: Original global blended DEM listed in source_dataset.original_asset
processing_pipeline.operation: Subset an approximate Jezero geographic bounding box, reproject to local Mars stereographic coordinates using bilinear resampling at 200 m pixel spacing, then derive slope with a central-difference gradient.
processing_pipeline.mathematical_method: slope_degrees = degrees(atan(sqrt((dz/dx)^2 + (dz/dy)^2))); gradients use 200 m horizontal spacing.

parameters.nodata_edge_exclusion: binary erosion of valid-data mask by one cell

known_limitations: The processing script does not independently verify the source DEM vertical unit before using elevation values in the gradient.
The source product record warns that some blended regions can contain interpolation or blending artifacts.
Slope from a 200 m/pixel raster is provisional and omits sub-pixel hazards.

processing_pipeline.operation: Classify each valid slope cell into four project-defined slope classes; preserve source grid alignment and mark NoData as code 0.

parameters.boundary_rule: Each class upper bound is inclusive; the next class lower bound is exclusive.

class_codes.2: Moderate slope, above 5 to 12 degrees inclusive
class_codes.3: High slope, above 12 to 18 degrees inclusive

known_limitations: Categories and thresholds are ARES project conventions, not NASA-certified rover-safety or traversability classes.
Slope class alone does not establish physical traversability.

processing_pipeline.output_product: route response generated per request; no route is stored as a fixed terrain product
processing_pipeline.operation: 8-directional A* over finite nonnegative slope cells. Cells above the request's maximum slope and NoData cells are blocked; diagonal movement requires both adjacent orthogonal cells to be traversable.
processing_pipeline.heuristic: Straight-line projected distance in metres; admissible because every edge cost is at least its geometric distance.

units.movement_cost: slope-weighted metre-equivalent, not energy or duration

parameters.maximum_slope_degrees: per request, greater than 0 and at most 90

known_limitations: The planner is a grid pathfinding demonstration, not autonomous rover navigation.
Slope is the only terrain cost and hard constraint; rover dynamics, rocks, wheel slip, soil and subsurface hazards are not modeled.

processing_pipeline.input_product: Calculated route cell sequence and jezero-slope-raster
processing_pipeline.output_product: terrain_profile field in the route response
processing_pipeline.operation: Summarize measured source-raster slope values at actual route cells into project-defined categories and calculate route-cell percentages and edge distances by category.

parameters.edge_distance_assignment: Each route edge is assigned to the more severe category of its two endpoint cells.
parameters.high_slope_segment_definition: A contiguous sequence of route cells above the moderate-class upper threshold.

known_limitations: Profile class membership is project-defined and does not imply safety or traversability.
Category edge distances use the documented endpoint attribution convention and are not separate measured surface distances.

generated_at.evidence: filesystem modification timestamp; no generation timestamp is embedded in the existing raster

derived_products.processing_stage: visualization-only; four rendered slope color bands

generated_at.evidence: filesystem modification timestamp; generated on demand by the API

derived_products.processing_stage: RGBA visualization of derived classification codes; not independent scientific measurements

scientific_limitations: Elevation vertical units have not been independently verified; derived slopes are provisional.
The source is a NASA/ESA blended DEM distributed by USGS, not exclusively NASA data.
The listed USGS product landing page is not evidence that the DEM appears in any particular challenge resource list.
Slope-only categories are project-defined and not NASA-certified traversability or rover safety thresholds.
A* route distance and slope-weighted movement cost do not represent energy consumption, travel time, or a validated rover mobility model.
No rocks, wheel-slip probabilities, soil properties, subsurface hazards, rover dynamics, or autonomous navigation behaviors are modeled.
The global source DEM checksum was intentionally not computed because the file is 11,384,463,908 bytes.
ai_assisted_development_disclosure: A Copilot-based AI assistant in VS Code assisted with software implementation, debugging, test authoring, quality checks, and technical documentation. At runtime, ARES does not call a generative-AI service. Illustrative scoring and the commander text response use deterministic local logic; terrain routes are calculated by the FastAPI backend from processed raster data. The repository does not establish whether visual assets were AI-generated; their origin must be confirmed by the project team before making an originality or AI-generation claim. Project authors remain responsible for reviewing the code, sources, and scientific claims. AI assistance does not imply NASA or USGS review, endorsement, validation, or challenge-rule compliance.
